rationale: Browser-harness is a highly relevant, actively maintained framework designed specifically for connecting LLM agents to browsers via CDP. Its architecture is minimal (~1k lines) but effective, emphasizing agent-driven skill development and self-improvement through an editable `agent-workspace`. It directly supports browser automation and provides primitives for screen recording and interaction, which are critical for scraping structured data. The tier A rating reflects its foundational utility, clear design for agent ergonomics, and direct applicability to the scraping pipeline.
limitations: Primarily designed as a harness for existing LLM-driven agents rather than a standalone scraping engine.
Relies on external browser instances (Chrome/Chromium via CDP) or Browser Use Cloud, requiring user-side setup.
Capabilities for structured data extraction are dependent on the agent's implemented domain skills.
